result.stdout:
dotcov - Cobertura coverage toolkit

One command's usage, options, and exit codes: dotcov <command> --help, or dotcov help <command>

Commands:
  dotcov report <path> [options]
      Parse and display coverage.
  dotcov check <path> --min-line N and/or --min-branch N [options]
      CI gate: exit 1 when line or branch coverage is below its minimum.
  dotcov crap <path> [options]
      CRAP gate, comp^2*(1-cov)^3+comp per method: exit 1 when any method scores strictly
      above --max-crap (at-threshold passes; default 30; every method must be scored).
  dotcov diff <before> <after> [options]
      Compare two reports: the files whose coverage changed, and a count of the rest.
  dotcov snapshot <path> [options]
      Create pipeline-ready JSON (identity defaults to 'unknown').
  dotcov test [<project>] --min-line N and/or --min-branch N [options] [-- <dotnet test arguments>]
      Run dotnet test with coverage into a fresh TestResults/<run>, then report and gate it
      like check.
  dotcov version, dotcov --version
      Show the version.
  dotcov help [<command>], dotcov <command> --help
      Show this help, or one command's usage, options, and exit codes.

Options (a command rejects any option it does not take, never ignores it):
  --format table|json|md    Output format (default table; markdown is the long name of md)
                            (report, check, crap, diff, test)
  --threshold N             Minimum the markdown verdict shows, 0 to 100; display only, never
                            the exit code
                            (report)
  --min-line N              Minimum line coverage, 0 to 100; 0 disables the dimension
                            (check, test)
  --min-branch N            Minimum branch coverage, 0 to 100; 0 disables the dimension
                            (check, test)
  --max-crap N              Highest CRAP score that passes (default 30)
                            (crap)
  --top N                   Show the N worst files (report) or methods (crap), or list at most N files
[truncated]
